exclusions: BJD_TDB/HJD/UTC conversion and observatory arrival times
Measured transit residuals and physical validity of long extrapolations
Nonzero period-epoch covariance, asymmetric errors, TTVs, orbital decay
Duration uncertainty, eccentric contact asymmetry, visibility and ranking accuracy
Leap-second elapsed-time arithmetic, overflow, and sub-ULP periods outside the bounded corpus
policy.failure_policy: Do not tune bounds from measured residuals. Unexpected numerical/topological failures block the benchmark; predeclared boundary indeterminacy and scientific unsupported states remain explicit in results.
policy.range_policy: Closed interval selecting midpoints, not overlap of padded windows. Exact dyadic boundaries must match exactly. Non-dyadic boundaries farther than the absolute-time bound must match exactly; inside the bound retain exact reference and actual topology as boundary_indeterminate, never count as independently validated topology. Grossly wrong epochs remain failures even in boundary cases.
policy.rationale: At astronomical JD a binary64 ULP is about 40 microseconds; the scalar bound permits input quantization and several arithmetic roundings. Duration subtracts two such dates. Uncertainty is computed without subtracting large JD values.
policy.reference: Independent Python decimal (60 significant digits), published linear ephemeris and NIST propagation law; no AstroScope or astronomy-library imports
policy.scope: Linear, constant-duration ephemeris arithmetic on one common time coordinate; not observed-transit accuracy or UTC/barycentric conversion
policy.uncertainty_policy: sigma(n)^2 = sigma_T0^2 + n^2 sigma_P^2 only under zero covariance; None is numerically zero but scientifically unknown, not proof of zero uncertainty. Constant T14 and symmetric contacts are model assumptions.
